analysis.session_summary: Friday's NFP beat (165K vs 65K) initially lifted USD +0.157% and Canada's employment miss (-4.7K vs 14.6K) weakened CAD -0.133%, but the USD rally was rejected after the prelim UoM beat printed inverted and USD gave back 72% of its peak. NZD closed at its best (+0.809%) with no own catalyst, while AUD selling was rejected and CAD ended weakest. Geopolitical headlines around Iran produced short-lived two-way moves, but most legs lacked a clear single trigger. The tape flags fragile USD longs and a risk bid led by NZD.

themes.theme: Risk-sensitive FX lead, commodity bloc split: NZD up, CAD down
themes.evidence: NZD closed at best +0.809%; CAD weakest -0.281% after jobs miss; AUD recovered 61% of dip.

themes.theme: US data beat fades; UoM inversion signals fragile USD longs
themes.evidence: NFP beat 165K vs 65K produced +0.157% USD impulse, but prelim UoM 51.0 vs 48.1 printed inverted -0.046% and USD gave back 72% of peak.

themes.theme: Geopolitical headlines chop risk but lack ownership
themes.evidence: Iran source positive added +8.1 pips to EUR/USD up leg; later Rubio not productive moved opposite but too weak to own moves.

currency_drivers.USD: Strong NFP beat lifted USD initially, but UoM beat printed inverted and gains faded.
currency_drivers.EUR: No own catalyst; drifted lower across the board as USD firmed.
currency_drivers.JPY: BOJ Ueda spoke without forecast; JPY softened 0.044% and move was unscored.
currency_drivers.GBP: No own catalyst; weakened modestly in risk-choppy trade.
currency_drivers.AUD: No own release; early selling rejected, recovered 61% of dip.
currency_drivers.CAD: Employment miss of -4.7K vs 14.6K weakened CAD; Ivey beat was muted.
currency_drivers.CHF: No own catalyst; underperformed as risk recovery reduced haven demand.
currency_drivers.NZD: No own release; closed at its best, leading G10 on risk appetite.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD opened with a 64.4-pip down leg amplified by NFP, then bounced 26.3 pips on Iran optimism before fading to close -36.7 pips; the up/down alternation shows no durable trend.

polarity_reads.read: Textbook USD strength (+0.157%) on strong jobs data, but failure to hold gains suggests the market was already long USD.
Inverted beat (USD weaker 0.046%) despite stronger sentiment implies positioning was short USD or market saw less need for Fed support.
CAD -0.133% on a clear labor miss indicates the market trusted the downside surprise and priced CAD weakness aggressively.
Unscored because no forecast; JPY softened 0.044% but that tells little about positioning.
Muted -0.007% basket move inside noise floor; CAD ignored the beat, suggesting no marginal information.

scenarios.name: Risk recovery extends; NZD/AUD outperform, USD stays soft
scenarios.thesis: NZD closed at its best (+0.809%) and AUD selling was rejected; Iran-positive headline and China tariff suspension suggest risk appetite can continue while USD longs remain fragile after UoM inversion.
triggers: China extends suspension of 24% US tariffs further
Iran mediation produces a concrete deal
scenarios.invalidation: Rubio-style 'talks not productive' headlines dominate and DXY closes back above 101.982

pair_paths.rationale: NZD closed at its best and has the strongest G10 momentum; 69.9-pip day range allows continuation.
AUD selling was rejected and recovered 61% of dip; risk recovery favors retest of 0.6888 close.
USD softness would allow EUR/USD to retrace the 36.7-pip decline within its 67.8-pip range.

scenarios.name: USD reasserts on rate differentials and Fed repricing
scenarios.thesis: The 165K vs 65K NFP beat was fundamentally strong even though the UoM inverted; once positioning clears, yield support can drive USD higher against EUR, GBP and JPY.
triggers: Fed speakers reiterate resilient economy (Williams: US economy remarkably resilient)
US yields rise and USD/CAD extends above 1.41034
scenarios.invalidation: EUR/USD recovers above its 1.11594 close and NZD/USD holds above 0.5597

pair_paths.rationale: The NFP-driven down leg was 64.4 pips; a clean USD bid would retest that move.
GBP had no own catalyst and its largest down leg was 77.8 pips; vulnerable to USD strength.
USD/JPY's largest up leg was 62.9 pips; higher US yields would push toward 158.23 close.
CAD labor miss is bearish CAD; USD/CAD up leg was 73.0 pips and close at 1.41034.

scenarios.name: Geopolitical headline-driven chop
scenarios.thesis: Iran and China headlines moved pairs both ways but no single trigger owned any leg; expect mean reversion within recent ranges as headlines remain two-sided.
triggers: Rubio: Talks Not Productive, Iranian Demands Simply Unacceptable
US warns China on Busan trade truce
BOE Bailey speaks and adds to GBP noise
scenarios.invalidation: A decisive break of EUR/USD 67.8-pip range or USD/JPY 88.1-pip range would signal a trend

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD closed within its 67.8-pip range after alternating up/down legs, consistent with chop.
USD/JPY range 88.1 pips with no clear catalyst; geopolitical headline risk keeps it two-sided.
EUR/GBP closed +0.5 pip with 18.3-pip range; both EUR and GBP lacked independent drivers.

risks.risk: Inverted UoM reaction indicates crowded USD positioning; a reversal could be violent
risks.why_it_matters: The market sold USD on strong consumer sentiment, suggesting longs were extended; unwinds can move EUR/USD and USD/JPY quickly.
risks.watch: Next US consumer confidence/inflation and Fed speak.

risks.risk: Iran deal headlines are two-sided and can reverse risk trades
risks.why_it_matters: A positive Iranian source moved risk pairs, but Rubio later said talks not productive; false signals can whipsaw NZD, AUD, and CHF.
risks.watch: Iran mediation updates and Rubio statements.

risks.risk: China tariff news directly hits AUD/NZD
risks.why_it_matters: The headline 'China to extend suspension of 24% US tariffs' moved AUD/NZD opposite to its prior uptrend; a breakdown would hit the commodity bloc.
risks.watch: China trade policy and US-China talks.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: Only BOE Gov Bailey Speaks is on the calendar ahead; no high-tier US releases. Bailey can shift GBP, but the dominant drivers remain geopolitical headlines and any China trade updates.
